newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary central bank calls for fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: Hungary central bank calls for fiscal discipline.

text.p: The Council of the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) on Friday warned the government not to increase 1998 budget expenditure targets and to keep wage and price increases at reasonable levels.
"In order to maintain sustainable economic growth, fiscal discipline is a determining factor," the Council said in a statement, concluding its meeting held earlier this week.
The Council said that it looked at the economic processes of the first quarter of 1997 and found that the acceleration of economic growth, seen in the second half of 1996, continued.
The figures of the first three months showed an improvement in the external and domestic balance of the economy, it said.
"In comparison with the programme, the expected pace of economic growth is seen quicker while the price increases of the first five months are lower," the Council said.
"However, with these favourable factors, points of tension are also seen in macroeconomic processes."

The lower than planned level of household savings, the quicker than targeted rise in nominal wages and the increase in the expected deficit of the social security funds are all signals calling for cautiousness, the statement said.

"To reach 1998 balance, growth and inflation targets, it is necessary to keep the 1998 budget targets and to keep wages and the prices of main products and services -- e.g. energy, telecommunications -- in line with 1998 inflation targets," it said.

According to the current plans, Hungary will reach a two percent surplus in the 1998 government budget excluding debt service expenditures and keep increased expenditure from 1997 at a maximum 16.5 percent. But there is intense pressure on the government to increase spending further.

The NBH warned that while economic growth is picking up, Hungary can cut inflation further only if the budget deficit does not rise, nominal wages and household savings are around the targets and the current account deficit is financed from foreign direct investment inflow and privatisation revenues.

Economic growth should be fueled by exports and also by investments mainly by the private sector, supported by exports and to a smaller extent by an increase in domestic demand, the central bank Council said.
It said the NBH would continue its cautious interest rate policies in the interest of reducing inflation and encouraging savings.
The Council agrees with the government decision to cut the monthly rate of the forint's crawling peg devaluation to one percent on August 15 from 1.1 percent, it said.
"And it sees an opportunity to cut the devaluation rate further next year if macroeconomic processes go according to the programme," it added.
